blocks.text: The harbour was quiet before the boats went out, and the gulls stood on the posts like people waiting for a bus.
Nell walked the length of the sea wall twice, counting the lamps, and then sat on the steps to watch the tide come in.
The storm came up from the south in the afternoon, grey at first and then the colour of slate.
By supper the windows rattled in their frames, and the fire leaned sideways in the grate whenever the door was opened.
The light turned all night, as it always had, though no ship came close enough to need it.
In the spring the painters came to give the tower a new white coat, and Nell carried their brushes up and down the stair.
The stair to the attic creaked on every third step, so that anyone climbing it played the same slow tune.
At the top the wind was so strong that she had to hold the rail with both hands and shout to be heard.
